entries.subject: Inspectable collective planning and dense reference execution

fields.Acceptance requirement: `collective.rs` provides deterministic semantic `DeviceId`/ordered `DeviceGroup`, broadcast, all-gather, reduce-scatter, and sum all-reduce plans plus a stepwise in-memory executor. It is tested across 1–4 devices, empty/uneven partitions, narrow storage, trace dependencies, and validation errors.

Sequential one-through-four-device sum all-reduce executes existing plan actions through primary pooled peer copies and typed add kernels against the deterministic mock. Every CUDA and in-memory executor revalidates the exact deterministic plan artifact before allocation or action submission, so tampered chunks/actions/dependencies/ranges/cache identity fail before mutation. Other collectives, overlap, narrow dtypes, NCCL/process transport, and live CUDA validation remain pending.

Not claimed. Checked-in tinygrad evidence is reduction-driven `ALLREDUCE` in `tinygrad/schedule/multi.py` and naive/ring/all-to-all schedule selection in `tinygrad/schedule/allreduce.py`; it is not a distributed-process API inventory.

entries.subject: Static tensor sharding layouts and exact reference data movement

fields.Acceptance requirement: `sharding.rs` implements immutable replicated/equal-axis layouts over the stable collective device group; validates ordered exact dense shards; and has exact `shard`/`gather`/replicate/redistribute reference movement. Evidence: checked-in `tinygrad/tensor.py::Tensor.shard` and `tinygrad/uop/ops.py::_shard`; uneven axis dimensions are rejected exactly as tinygrad does. Static movement and collective-lowering decisions are inspectable independently of Graph/runtime execution.

`sharded_graph.rs` validates graph-bound local node wrappers and composes shrink/concat gather, explicit redistribution, local elementwise/select/movement, sharded-axis sum/mean, and rank-two matmul through the existing CPU/reverse-mode graph semantics. Local binary traces retain ordered per-rank operand/provenance records for future transfer-to-local fusion; canonical schedule-buffer attachment, CUDA scheduling, lazy multi-device realization, and runtime collectives remain Phase 3 boundaries.

`sharded_cuda_plan.rs` validates semantic-device/primary-owner/capability bindings and serializes local schedule/PTX cache stages plus trace-derived transfer/all-reduce stages without entering CUDA or materializing data. It retains renderable static elementwise/select/cast, exact Neg/Abs, and static reduction stages; graph-specific reduction/matmul and every unsupported renderer contract remain explicit diagnostics carrying the renderer reason. Driver allocation, streams, module load, and launch remain Phase 3B.

Graph-derived local Add has cache/oracle evidence across 1/2/4 owners for F32/I32/U64, including canonical zero routes. Static-view cast, broadcasted boolean select, and exact I32/F32 `GraphUnary` Neg execute through the generic semantic Mock across 1/2/4 owners; Neg retains original view-source bindings, owner-scoped cache isolation, and logical zero-domain no-work behavior. Unsupported unary/dtype pairs remain typed diagnostics. Typed transfer→local composition substitutes exact descriptor-matched outputs into local inputs and preserves a validated dependency DAG; direct provenance fusion validates explicit external-materialized ABI order and has CPU-byte evidence for 1/2/4-owner axis→replicated Add, 2-owner axis0→axis1 Add, and zero-domain no-work execution. Computed-shrink broadcast, collectives, and live CUDA remain pending.

Typed graph-derived two/four-owner axis-to-replicated, replicated-to-axis, and axis-to-axis routes validate ordered owners, layouts, graph-buffer identities, dtype, and checked element/byte ranges before exact mock execution. Same-owner DtoD and cross-owner peer transfers retain deterministic route order; injected DtoD/peer failures restore external sources for retry, including composed local execution. Retained-allocator stat assertions, collectives, and live CUDA remain pending.

entries.subject: Dense data, scalars and shape validation

fields.Acceptance requirement: Valid/invalid storage tests

Adam/LAMB checkpoint restoration uses full-width bias correction and rejects a final `u64` step overflow before state or parameter mutation. Checked static `diagonal` lowers through permutation plus existing `StaticIndex` for signed axes/offsets, rectangular/batched/zero/Bool cases. F32/F64 CPU-JIT `exp2` is strict native lowering with a renderer cache-version update; narrow floats reject. `FileBuffer::read_tensor_file` bounds metadata bytes and item-size alignment before copying a flat canonical little-endian rank-one `TensorData`, including empty files. `save_tensor_file` encodes complete canonical bytes before exclusively staging and syncing a same-directory file, then changes the target only by final rename and cleans only its own failed staging. These are bounded host/static surfaces: no dynamic indexing, broad JIT transcendental family, mmap/lazy/device backing, or optimizer/device redesign.

F16/BF16 public sums accumulate and return F32. Checked `SplitSizes` drives static `split`/`chunk` solely through existing `Shrink` views, while checked static `unfold` creates only validated sliding `Shrink` windows; both preserve signed axes and zero-domain distinctions. `Graph::cumsum` is an inclusive checked static single-axis `PrefixScan`: integer/bool inputs use default sum promotion; F16/BF16/Float8 retain source dtype; scalar and zero-extent domains are exact. Its typed UOp/RGUA payload has CPU-oracle schedule/materialization/cache evidence only. Floating `cumsum` reverse mode composes reverse-scan-reverse over the stored normalized axis and retains graph-on-graph seed edges; `cumprod` and non-floating `cumsum` gradients reject before derivative graph mutation. Fixed-size `masked_select(size, fill)` separately reuses boolean prefix ranks only as nondifferentiable control to route an explicit upstream cotangent to retained row-major source lanes. Mask/index control, padding/truncation/false lanes, dynamic cardinality, CPU-JIT, PTX/OpenCL/Metal/WebGPU, parallel scans, and replay widening remain excluded. `var`/`var_mean`/`std`/`std_mean` compose existing mean/square/cast/sum nodes with F32-or-F64 accumulation and checked correction; Float8 variance rejects before graph mutation. `ones_with_dtype`, `const_like`, implicit random-like helpers, and typed `randperm_implicit` reuse captured Threefry reservations. `StaticIndexGrad`, `StaticIndexUpdateGrad`, and `ScatterPositionsVjp` reuse normalized static maps or static scatter positions for bounded graph-on-graph reverse construction. Einsum removes presentation whitespace before the existing parser; rearrange accepts Unicode identifiers but rejects empty sides before mutation. Directional `isinf` composes canonical predicates with typed sign comparisons; `hardswish` uses its source-matching ReLU6 composition; empty `logsumexp` has its local `-inf` identity; and accepted tinygrad scalar dtype aliases normalize to existing canonical `DType`s. Static `tril`/`triu` mask final two axes and supply causal attention through the same select composition. UOp scalar literals validate exact dtype/width in direct and artifact forms, while pure Add folds only type-matched positive raw zero and retains negative-zero literals. These are static CPU Graph surfaces only: no new runtime/IR/backend, dynamic shapes, device lowering, effect indexing, or broad dtype claim.

Exact integral/bool UOp identity rewrites preserve floating signed-zero/NaN lanes; `TensorData::bitcast` reinterprets only equal-width canonical raw bytes. CPU float extrema retain the left operand on unordered/tied lanes, and softplus/mish/logsigmoid use stable finite-tail composition. Graph `any`/`all` have typed empty identities; `Graph::masked_fill` is only the existing checked Bool-mask `select(mask, value, input)` composition, retaining its broadcasting, promotion, trace, and reverse-mode behavior. Seeded Graph dropout reuses existing random/select operations. `SafetensorsReadLimits` bounds owned local reads before the canonical parser, while writes exclusively stage and sync a same-directory temporary before rename, clean their own failed staging, and never open an existing target for writing. `Conv1d` joins the existing static `ModuleForward` seam through its canonical NCL-to-Conv2d lowering and OIW state; `AvgPool2d` and `MaxPool2d` remain bounded seam members. `Schedule::validate` rejects noncanonical IDs/dependencies/consumer mirrors before planning, realization, or capture. These are bounded static CPU and artifact-integrity semantics only, with no new scheduler/runtime, trainer, device, dynamic-shape, or generic parity claim.

entries.subject: Static diag, native Sin, and transpose-conv modules

fields.Acceptance requirement: `Graph::diag` accepts rank-one inputs only, checks `n + 1`/`n²` before graph mutation, and composes existing unsqueeze, typed-zero pad, flatten, shrink, and reshape for exact zero `[0,0]` and raw-dtype behavior. Strict CPU JIT lowers `Sin` only for F32/F64 with deterministic scalar/vector cache identities and captured replay reuse; F16/BF16 reject and `Tan` remains unsupported. `ConvTranspose2d::new_static` is graph-independent, its legacy constructor delegates exactly, and its `ModuleForward` adapter only uses the existing static NCHW Graph lowering with configured channels. No broad diagonal/indexing, native model/device, transpose-conv geometry, runtime/IR, or dynamic claim is added.

entries.subject: Static cumprod, native Trunc, and 1D transpose-conv modules

fields.Acceptance requirement: `Graph::cumprod` shares typed static `PrefixScan` Sum/Product payloads with `cumsum`: one checked signed axis, exact scalar/zero extent behavior, CPU schedule/UOp/RGUA identity, and source dtype retention including Bool; v11 PrefixScan artifacts decode as Sum and the effect envelope is v13. Strict CPU JIT lowers `Trunc` only for F32/F64 with exact signed-zero CPU parity and deterministic scalar/vector captured-replay cache identity; F16/BF16 reject and `Cos` remains unsupported. `ConvTranspose1d::new_static` is graph-independent, legacy construction delegates exactly, and its `ModuleForward` path only reuses the existing static NCL-to-2D Graph lowering with configured channels. Scan autograd/JIT/device lowering, broader transpose-conv workflows, runtime/IR, and dynamic claims remain absent.

entries.subject: Signed-zero Abs and atomic scheduler state

fields.Acceptance requirement: CPU `Abs` preserves a F16/BF16/F32/F64 input negative-zero lane, matching tinygrad's observable `x * sign(x)` behavior; ordinary finite, infinity, NaN, dtype, and existing Abs VJP semantics are unchanged, while Float8 remains separate. Every host scheduler validates the next `u64` epoch before state mutation, and `LrSchedulerGroup` steps cloned scheduler/optimizer candidates before one all-or-nothing commit, so any child error preserves all child epochs and learning rates. This adds no weak dtype, Float8, optimizer family, trainer, runtime, or device behavior.

Public `LiteralScalar::{Bool,I64,U64,F64}` lets `Graph::constant_literal`, `binary_literal`, and `literal_binary` resolve an untyped scalar immediately to ordinary concrete scalar `TensorData` against a strong peer dtype. Signed zero remains distinct while NaN identity is canonical; integer conversion uses the existing checked tinygrad-compatible wrapping route, F64 follows a float peer or F32, and bool-peer integers resolve I32. No weak `DType`, storage, UOp, artifact, cache key, explicit typed `TensorData` API change, runtime, or device behavior is introduced.
Matrix/row/scalar cases

Static dense `full/zeros/ones/empty`, integer `arange`, `linspace`, `eye`, all static `*_like` forms, `randperm`, scaled/Glorot/Kaiming uniform/normal initializers, `one_hot`, and `meshgrid` are CPU-tested. The CPU oracle has a typed U32 Threefry2x32 core with checked source vectors, carry-safe chunk planning, and raw F16/BF16/F32/F64 unit-interval construction. `manual_seed` safely resets a mutex-serialized registry of captured per-device stream reservations; each implicit random node records its key/counter so replay is independent of execution scheduling, including `randperm`'s F32 random-key reservation, packed narrow-float, odd-word, empty, and cross-call accounting. Captured schedules retain a typed random UOp plan and serialize its exact reservation; graph-free interpreter and strict native C replay cover static uniform (F16/BF16/F32/F64), tinygrad's paired F32-source Box--Muller normal (F16/BF16/F32/F64), and the F32 uniform-scale-then-cast `randint` route for all public integer storage dtypes. Native rendering uses the immutable key/counter reservation only; it neither reads nor mutates the stream registry. CUDA PTX lowers captured static uniform/normal F16 (sm_53+), BF16, F32, and F64 plus F32-uniform-scale `randint` for every public integer storage dtype through immutable Threefry payloads and owner-scoped exact semantic mocks. PTX normal uses target approximate transcendentals, so live CUDA comparison is tolerance-only; no live CUDA/ptxas evidence is claimed. Accelerator state reservation and live accelerator validation remain explicit boundaries. Numeric device `0` uses tinygrad's first-device SHA-derived key; other numeric device IDs use documented deterministic distinct keys because RustGrad has no canonical backend-device name layer yet. Explicit seed APIs remain supported as a separate stateless compatibility contract. Remaining names are `const_like`, implicit aliases for every initializer, and initializer families requiring QR/linalg or sparse/convolution layouts. RustGrad `empty` deterministically zero-initializes instead of exposing allocator contents.

entries.subject: Bool, integer, fp16/bf16/fp32/f64 and special dtypes

fields.Acceptance requirement: Dense tagged storage includes bool/i8-u64/f16/bf16/f32/f64 plus raw-bit-preserving float8 `E4M3`, `E5M2`, `E4M3FNUZ`, and `E5M2FNUZ`. **Float8 C6/C7 CPU oracle:** MatMul and Conv2d use their source-audited multiply-then-sum F32 accumulation with a single final narrow; Conv2d bias is then applied at its typed graph boundary. Static Einsum preserves raw storage for verified single-input diagonal-free reorders; its contractions use F32-step product/add accumulation and one final Float8 narrowing when the promoted result is Float8. Cross-format float8 and wider-float operands use the established promotion lattice. Accumulating scatter-add, padding, arg reductions, random, autograd, CPU JIT, PTX/OpenCL/Metal/WebGPU/CUDA, and device ABI lowering remain fail-closed for float8.

entries.subject: Unary, binary, comparison and transcendental ALU

fields.Acceptance requirement: CPU primitives inventory includes add/sub/mul/div, neg, exp/log/exp2/log2, abs/reciprocal/square/sqrt/rsqrt, sin/cos/tan/sinh/cosh/tanh, erf/erfc, asin/acos/atan/atan2, asinh/acosh/atanh, copysign, relu, floor/ceil/trunc/round/sign, isnan/isinf/isfinite, pow, maximum/minimum, floor/trunc division, floor/C remainder, bitwise and/or/xor and shifts; comparisons, bool logic and broadcasted select are verified. Dtype matrix: predicates return bool for every stored dtype; float-only unary math promotes bool and all integer types to F32, while F16/BF16/F32/F64 retain and re-quantize their dtype; neg/relu/step/abs/square/rounding/sign retain exact bool/integer storage; binary operations use the checked-in tinygrad least-upper lattice (including signed/unsigned widening and F16+BF16→F32). Bool bitwise is AND/OR/XOR; shifts require a non-bool integer result type. Integer division/remainder by zero return `DivisionByZero`; signed MIN/-1 uses wrapping arithmetic. Shift counts must be `0 <= count < result bit width`; this deliberate CPU-oracle divergence narrows tinygrad's renderer-dependent out-of-range shift behavior. Float special values, inverse-function domains, copysign signed-zero/NaN semantics, and F16/BF16 construction/cast/unary/binary/reduction quantization are regression-tested. Float reverse mode covers smooth primitives (including special functions and atan2) plus pow broadcasting/zero guards and 50/50 extrema ties; copysign differentiates its magnitude only, matching tinygrad's predicate-based sign contract.

Unified static-axis sum/mean/product/min/max and argmin/argmax support all/signed multi-axis selection and keepdim, with CPU exact storage. Focused CPU regressions verify NaN-ignoring extrema, even tie shares, zero-aware product gradients, finite differences away from nondifferentiable points, typed empty sum/mean/product behavior, explicit empty extrema/arg errors, and `ReduceGrad` trace shape/dtype. Full tinygrad dtype-accumulation and dynamic/symbolic reduction coverage remain.

CPU-oracle generalized dense matmul supports rank-1 dot, matrix/vector forms, and broadcasted batch dimensions with promoted dense dtypes. `MatmulKernelPlan` owns normalized semantics; eligible nonempty F32 matrix forms carry a serialized deterministic `TiledMatmulPlan` and shared-memory PTX. Exact-tile homogeneous F16/BF16 matrices carry a serialized sm_80+ `TensorCoreMatmulPlan` with one-warp m16n8k16 row/col fragments, F32 accumulation, and one narrow-output requantization. Exact-representable simulator/oracle fixtures are covered; broad bitwise equivalence to the F64 oracle is not claimed. A separate `QuantizedMatmulPlan` covers F32 vector/batched activations times read-only Llama-orientation `[N,K]` Q4_0/Q8_0/Q4_K/Q6_K weights. Its independent reference and native C path decode blocks inside K accumulation, use f64 accumulation/final F32 storage, and never allocate a dense weight. K must be block-exact; K=0 is defined. Quantized backward, other formats/orientations, tiled quantized kernels, quantized PTX/device execution, tensor-core tails/multi-warp scheduling, empirical autotuning, and live-CUDA validation remain gaps. `MatmulGradVjp` retains dense second-order coverage; linalg beyond matmul remains.

CPU-oracle NCHW/OIHW Conv2d is acceptance-tested. **Static pooling is ✅ complete:** general trailing-spatial `max_pool`/`avg_pool` support arbitrary-rank options, including checked-in 3D tuple usage, and 2D wrappers delegate to the same normalized core. Generalized max indices return checked I32 flattened original-spatial indices with earliest-index ties; NaN, padding, dilation, ceil windows, divisors, and split-tie value gradients are acceptance-tested. Pooling behavior is validated from checked-in source and RustGrad's CPU oracle; only a live tinygrad runtime differential remains unavailable in this workspace. Winograd and broader convolution-family work remain.

Checked shrink/signed slicing, integer gather, deterministic replacement scatter, and scatter-add exist. `ir::indexing` provides typed immutable static mixed indexing (integer/slice/newaxis/ellipsis and constant broadcasted integer tensors), checked static sliding `unfold`, a narrow plan-carrying Graph op, CPU execution, and duplicate-accumulating F32 reverse scatter. `Graph::static_index_update` is a functional snapshot update with exact same-dtype RHS broadcasting and row-major last-writer-wins duplicates over bool/integer/narrow-float/float storage; its F32 VJPs use the plan's final-writer map, and `StaticIndexUpdateGrad` composes the same normalized static map for bounded higher-order seed derivatives. `EffectGraph::static_index_assign` carries that same normalized plan in typed STORE/AFTER payloads and atomically commits immutable target snapshots through `EffectRuntime`, including signed slices, advanced duplicates, RHS broadcasting, and raw narrow-float lanes. `EffectMutationPermit` performs a graph-derived first-order backward-slice analysis and binds a safe result to one exact target state: guarded whole, affine, and indexed effect assignments reject before STORE construction when the old pure value is needed by the requested backward slice; detached/no-grad, non-differentiable-only, and unrelated targets are classified safely. RGSM v2 serializes validated normalized index maps for graph-free interpreter replay against caller-owned effect state; malformed, stale, live-borrow, or injected failures preflight/abort without partial mutation, while RGSM v1 remains decodable. The permit is host/interpreter-only and is neither a persistent alias registry nor an effect VJP. Pure/effect mutation autograd beyond this static graph transform, native/device indexed-effect replay, and effect batches remain separate. Dense host `TensorData::assign_from` provides same-dtype whole-buffer broadcast assignment with snapshot source reads and transactional failure. `ir::dynamic` adds CPU-oracle `nonzero` with a typed rank/dtype contract and realization-time `[count, rank]` shape; its separately documented unbounded masked-select path is not a general dynamic indexing API. Static index values currently validate out-of-bounds eagerly, deliberately differing from tinygrad's zero-filled advanced-index read behavior. General dynamic boolean indexing and JIT/device lowering remain separate boundaries.

entries.subject: Mask, pad, concat, stack and split

fields.Acceptance requirement: Constant typed padding, multi-input concat with promotion, and fixed-size `masked_select(size, fill)` remain compatible. Its static reverse edge broadcasts/flattens the boolean mask, uses `PrefixScan` ranks only as nondifferentiable control indices, safely gathers explicit upstream cotangents for retained row-major lanes, and zeros padded, truncated, and false lanes; the mask and size have no gradient. The typed dynamic-result CPU oracle realizes `nonzero` and unbounded `masked_select_dynamic`, including checked bool-mask broadcasting and exact runtime shapes. `DynamicAllocationPlan` and the canonical typed `MixedSchedule` lower only CPU `masked_select_dynamic`, optional F32 `Neg`/`Square`, then one F32 `Add`/`Sub`/`Mul` with a checked static scalar, or scalar `Sum`/forward-only `Mean`, with exact runtime allocations, ordered bindings, lifetimes, and no placeholder capacity. Dynamic-to-dynamic binary composition, higher order, dynamic-mean autograd, general dynamic Graph composition/`Graph::grad`, non-scalar broadcast, generic runtime-to-fixed consumers, capture/artifact/replay/native JIT/PTX/device lowering remain explicit boundaries. Stack and split remain.

entries.subject: Reshape, permute, expand, shrink, stride and contiguous views

fields.Acceptance requirement: Materialized reshape/permute/expand, signed `unsqueeze`/`squeeze`/`flatten`, compositional `stack`, checked shrink, signed stride, and reverse-mode movement mappings exist. `ScatterPositionsVjp` closes second-order static shrink/pad/stride movement adjoints; true views and remaining movement ops remain.

Static dense `einsum` has a normalized inspected plan plus CPU forward and reverse oracle for arbitrary operand count, explicit/implicit output, ASCII labels, ellipses, repeated-label diagonals, broadcast-compatible labeled dimensions, scalar and zero-sized domains, and promoted storage. Float8 CPU einsum preserves raw storage for verified single-input diagonal-free reorders; contraction equations use tinygrad's aligned product then sum model with F32-step product/add accumulation and one final Float8 narrowing when the promoted result is Float8. `EinsumGradVjp` reuses that normalized plan for second-order upstream and non-target operand derivatives, preserving diagonal and broadcast scatter accumulation. Third-order indexed-contraction derivatives remain an explicit boundary. Static `rearrange` supports tinygrad's one-arrow identifier grammar with whitespace, `() / 1` singleton axes, non-nested parenthesized split/merge groups, Unicode/ASCII ellipsis, and named static factors (one inferred group factor); it lowers to reshape/permute and inherits their reverse mode. `repeat`/`tile` and scalar-count `repeat_interleave` lower through reshape/expand, including zero repetitions and gradient accumulation. Per-element repeat tensors and symbolic/dynamic output lengths, nested groups, and remaining rearrange features are unimplemented. Stable `logsumexp`, `softmax`, `log_softmax`, and compositional scaled dot-product attention support signed/static axes, narrow-float calculation control, bool/additive/causal masks, and static GQA head replication with first-order reverse mode. Training dropout supports inverted scaling through an explicit `dropout_seed`; eval mode bypasses it.

Portable checked little-endian dense bytes and safetensors state dictionaries (in-memory and atomic filesystem APIs) are implemented. Float8 `E4M3`, `E5M2`, `E4M3FNUZ`, and `E5M2FNUZ` are dense `TensorData` storage/transport dtypes with exact raw payload retention; only standard E4M3/E5M2 safetensors tags are emitted, while FNUZ and all NPY float8 descriptors reject. No float8 compute, zero-copy computation, mutable aliasing, NumPy/DLPack objects, device/mmap backing, or autograd alias semantics are claimed. Fail-closed Torch ZIP and legacy ustar TAR state-dict importers accept bounded protocol-2 CPU dense tensors through a no-code-execution pickle whitelist, retaining raw storage bits and validating non-overlapping stride reconstruction before materialization. `TorchStateReadLimits` adds bounded local ZIP-state reads and strict preconfigured-module loading through the existing all-lock transaction. `interop::host` provides dtype-agnostic signed-stride descriptors plus lifetime/Arc-bound read views and lifetime-bound injective write views without pointer or capacity escape. Canonical little-endian host bytes copy in row-major logical order to independent `TensorData` and transactionally from it, preserving raw bool/integer/float bits including narrow floats, NaNs, and signed zero. Its deterministic copy-based NPY v1/v2 encoder/decoder supports C- and Fortran-order materialized Bool, signed/unsigned integer, F16, F32, and F64 arrays; writer output is C-order little-endian. `load_npy_file_with_limits` bounds local file/header/rank/element inputs, and `save_npy_file` stages and syncs a same-directory replacement. BF16 and big/native-endian, object/string/structured/subarray/datetime/Unicode NPY descriptors fail closed. A bounded default-domain opset-13 ONNX CPU inference slice lowers concrete initializers and embedded tensor attributes; common arithmetic, predicates, selection and unary math; static Clip and inference-only no-op Dropout; Shape, Expand, Tile, same-rank constant-index Gather, constant-control Slice, positive constant-mode Pad, ConstantOfShape, static ReduceSum/Mean/Prod/Min/Max, and first-tie ArgMax/ArgMin; static NCHW 2D Conv; inference-only BatchNormalization; GlobalAveragePool; and static 2D float MaxPool/AveragePool. Local ONNX file workflows bound model reads, require exact named NPY input schemas before CPU execution, and stage selected named NPY outputs. Dynamic/control-flow/custom-domain, external data, dynamic indexing/pads/slices/reduction axes, Pad crop/reflect/edge, general-rank Gather, last-tie ArgMin/ArgMax, MaxPool index outputs/storage-order variants, BatchNormalization training/stat outputs, nonzero/training Dropout, CUDA/sparse/quantized/custom objects, NumPy/DLPack, device/mmap-backed tensors, and autograd alias semantics remain separate boundaries.
Initial ops and trace verified

entries.subject: Universal IR for ALU, memory, ranges and control

fields.Acceptance requirement: The immutable typed UOp DAG covers constants/vconsts, definitions, special/range/if delimiters, selected ALU/cast/vector/index/load/store/barrier/sink families, plus separate validated serial, scalar-tiled, and tensor-core Matmul payloads reusing normalized `MatmulKernelPlan`. Versioned node-table artifacts preserve and validate complete tile/capability/resource/barrier/fragment metadata. Full tinygrad op vocabulary and broader kernel lowering remain.

entries.subject: Symbolic integers, variables, bounds and shapes

fields.Acceptance requirement: Checked `i64` constants/identity-bearing variables, add/sub/neg/mul, floor div/mod, min/max, predicates, boolean/select, conservative bounds, strict bindings, symbolic broadcast/reshape products, and concrete graph specialization are tested. Serialized capture schemas preserve stable IDs/names, I64 domains, equality/divisibility guards, symbolic buffer shapes, elementwise/reduction/matmul domains, and source-backed affine view shapes/strides/offsets; checked Graph-free specialization is cached by canonical bindings. Exact-splat constants may resize by repeating one raw scalar pattern. Dynamic rank/cardinality, arbitrary constant resizing, control flow, device launches, tinygrad range/index values, and full UOp symbolic coverage remain.

Symbolic and UOp typed deterministic match/rewrite drivers record traces; phase-one UPat supports op sets, dtypes, arguments, source patterns and named captures. Full tinygrad UPat varargs, predicates and compiler-pattern IR remain.
Constant/identity folding, associative canonicalization, bound-proved comparisons and boolean normalization are tested; tinygrad's modular-congruence and transcendental rewrite suites remain.

Producer-aware schedule DAG/lazy realization records interpreter/native-JIT/fallback traces. `ExecutionPlanSummary` exposes a deterministic non-executing static Schedule plus logical `MemoryPlan` view for requested CPU-session outputs: descriptors, item identities/kinds, temporary/reuse counts, logical peaks, and zero-domain/sentinel facts only. `infer_module_native_cpu_with_report` is a separate static-F32 strict-native module opt-in: it retains the same detached result and strict preflight while exposing existing trace/cache/zero facts, a no-reuse canonical static summary, and nondeterministic current-call local durations for graph/schedule/capture, native preparation, and detached execution. It is not a profiler, benchmark, global counter, per-kernel timer, RSS/allocator/device-memory, or cache-resource metric. Static matmul is an executable materialization root with ordered bindings; eligible F32 matrices retain deterministic scalar-tiled selection, while exact-tile F16/BF16 matrices retain deterministic tensor-core selection and derived MemorySpacePlan shared/fragment lifetimes. Unsupported forms retain serial payloads. Computed operands, dependencies, consumers, and temporary lifetimes remain explicit. Generation-checked HostSlotPool leases/views/detached outputs and exact-compatible MemoryPlan reuse are alias-safe. Target ISA SIMD, tiled reductions, tensor-core padding/multi-warp search, empirical search, timing/RSS/device-memory counters, and runtime cache metrics remain boundaries.

Source-backed static shrink, contiguous reshape, permutation, expansion, and signed-stride chains lower through canonical `AffineView`/`ViewBufferIndex` across schedule, interpreter, native CPU replay, PTX, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU. Computed-value, unsupported signed reshape compositions, and non-affine chains remain explicit lowering boundaries.

entries.subject: Memory planning, reuse, subbuffers and alias safety

fields.Acceptance requirement: `MemoryPlan` has deterministic checked HostDense temporary lifetimes and exact-compatible reuse, while generation-checked HostSlot leases prevent stale logical views. `EffectPlan` and canonical UOp STORE/AFTER lower whole-buffer CPU assignments into deterministic effect-boundary `ScheduleItem`s. `EffectRuntime` owns HostSlot-backed logical buffer generations and atomically commits fully preflighted assignments from immutable snapshots; raw dtype, empty sentinel, chain, diamond, stale, and retry cases are tested. Typed `schedule::mixed` bindings feed pure outputs and versioned persistent snapshots, including checked signed `AffineView` reads, into the same transaction. `CapturedMixedSchedule` retains bounded/checksummed RGSM state/value ABI sidecars. `CapturedMixedBatch` has graph-free in-memory interpreter and strict-native CPU ordered replay: all captures stage rebased candidates privately and one `EffectRuntime::execute_batch` commit makes final states visible together. Batch serialization, devices, mutation autograd/live-use rules, and invalid rebinding schemas remain boundaries; validated total/bijective descriptor/version-compatible rebinding is released. Native traces exclude runtime slots, generations, pointers, and bytes. Ordinary RGSA artifacts still reject effects. Canonical signed `AffineView` carries ordinary late-IR views and checked negative-stride effect targets; writable maps remain injective-only. `AliasLivenessPlan` retains base/view/version lifetimes and never assigns aliases reusable temporary slots.

`RGMB` is a bounded, checksummed, deterministic ordered envelope of canonical RGSM entries. Decoding validates every embedded RGSM and the recomputed logical batch identity before interpreter or strict-native in-memory replay. `RGBS` packages exact version-zero raw `TensorData` beside byte-identical RGMB; its bounded decode validates the state frontier before a caller-selected validated total/bijective `MixedStateRebinding` atomically registers a fresh host `EffectRuntime`. The resulting bundle replays through interpreter, strict native, or the retained PTX semantic mock without state-byte migration or destination/runtime-resource serialization. A backend-neutral prepared-prefix coordinator drives OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and CUDA/PTX adapters, executing detached prefixes before one host transaction commits effects. There is no CPU fallback, device-resident persistent state, compiled-resource serialization, arbitrary historical/process-memory checkpointing, or live CUDA/toolkit mixed-batch evidence. F16/BF16 packed writes, F64/I64/U64, raw narrow indexed-duplicate source coverage, invalid/incompatible rebinding schemas, mutation autograd/live-use rules, and unsupported UOps remain gaps.
IR-to-IR transform covers current ALU, movement, reductions and first-order dedicated primitives. `grad_with` supplies explicit upstream validation and `create_graph` control.

Broadcast/reduction and finite-difference checks exist, including selection gradients through value branches plus product/extrema gradients across multi-axis and keepdim cases; predicates are intentionally nondifferentiable. Sum/mean, zero-aware product, max/min tie routing, reshape/permute/expand/shrink/pad/stride/concat, gather/scatter-add and select value branches retain second-order graph edges. `ReduceGradVjp` preserves product zero-count branches and extrema upstream routing; `ScatterPositionsVjp` preserves static movement adjoints. Floating `cumsum` uses the compositional reverse-scan-reverse edge with normalized-axis, scalar/empty, and graph-on-graph seed support; product scans and non-floating sum scans reject before derivative graph mutation. Fixed-size masked selection routes explicit upstream value cotangents through a static boolean prefix-rank map and keeps graph-on-graph seed routing; masks, sizes, and the prefix ranks remain nondifferentiable.

Generalized `MatmulGradVjp`, normalized-plan `EinsumGradVjp`, `Conv2dGradVjp`, and `ConvTranspose2dGradVjp` provide inspectable second-order VJPs for their corresponding value contractions. Convolution VJPs reuse grouped stride/dilation/padding coordinate maps; transpose convolution includes output padding and 1D inherits the singleton-height lowering. Pooling is compositional: average pooling differentiates normally and max pooling inherits the explicit tie/NaN `ReduceGradVjp` contract. Compositional attention paths backpropagate through query/key/value and are covered by finite fixtures.

Gradient paths accumulate by graph addition. Inputs carry explicit tracking state; `detach` shares values while stopping its edge; `no_grad` is scoped per graph and panic-safe. Host-only parameters bind by stable identity/current version into graph-local captured leaves; old graphs retain old values, tied handles share one leaf per version, and optimizer gradients carry identity/version stamps. Host-interpreter `EffectSourceBridge` records graph-local frozen provenance and `MutationTapeRecord` provides first-order F32 local replacement VJPs for whole, injective signed-affine, and normalized static-index writes, with broadcast-reduced RHS output gradients and explicit `Graph::grad_with` handoff. Persistent leaf `.grad` buffers, `EffectGraph::grad`, higher-order/capture/native/device mutation AD, and global mutable aliases are not part of the static graph API.

Smooth unary/binary expressions, broadcasting, ordinary movement, sum/mean/product/max/min, gather/scatter-add, select value branches, generalized matmul/einsum, convolution, transpose convolution, compositional pooling, and fixed-size masked-select seed routing support graph-on-graph second derivatives. Third-order dedicated contractions/reductions/movement/convolution, broader masked-select differentiation, and replacement scatter remain explicit boundaries.

Verified for implemented ops. `CpuSession` is the documented CPU-only public workflow: it owns explicit Graph bindings and session-validated tensor handles, realizes through this oracle, exposes graph traces, supports the existing first-order pure gradient transform, and rejects non-CPU session devices instead of falling back. Its bounded Phase B delegates static `sub/div`, ReLU, matmul, signed-axis softmax/argmax, permute/transpose, shrink/signed slice, concat, and integer gather to the existing Graph contracts. Phase C adds `CpuModuleTrainer`: fresh graph per static F32 `ModuleForward` sparse-classification train/evaluate request, evaluated parameter gradients through existing optimizer/scheduler ownership, and inspectable loss/logits/trace/version metadata. `infer_module_cpu` is the complementary graph-free static one-input inference path: each call snapshots current trainable parameters into a fresh CPU graph and returns detached output, trace, and canonical version metadata without mutation. `summarize_classification` supplies pure first-tie predictions/counts/optional accuracy for rank-two F32 logits and integer targets. No dynamic or device session fallback, generic trainer/data loader, mixed precision, runtime module-name dispatch, or metric-driven scheduler stepping is claimed.

`CpuJitBackend` provides cached native execution for Graph outputs and a validated `ScheduleItem` seam used by serialized replay. Process-local compilation is keyed by deterministic rendered identity and repeated artifact replay reports cache hits. Scalar/contiguous-vector elementwise, reductions, and homogeneous F32/F64 generalized matmul cover zero domains, vector tails, broadcast batches, multi-item dependencies, aligned contiguous views, legal strided scalar views, and vector scalar splats; native `Neg` is defined for Bool as logical-not and for signed widths as modulo unsigned subtraction with a bit-preserving signed result. F32/F64 `log2` lowers through the strict native lane path, while narrow storage rejects. Misaligned/non-affine views, native narrow/integer matmul, tiling, target-ISA SIMD, and unsupported transcendental families remain explicit unsupported/fallback boundaries.

entries.subject: CUDA Driver API runtime, allocator and copies

fields.Acceptance requirement: Runtime-loaded Driver API; owned and retained primary contexts, buffers, synchronous copies, streams/events and module/launch handles are mock-tested. Successful null graph/graph-exec/module/function outputs reject before ownership or launch; peer copies require their own optional symbol; and a failed mock stream wait preserves retryable owned resources. `PrimaryPoolStats` reports one exact allocator handle, with `pool_id` distinguishing separate pools on one owner and clones sharing state. The deterministic mock models owner-scoped primary device bytes, including colliding raw handles, and applies async HtoD/DtoH/DtoD and peer-copy bytes at submission while preserving event readiness behavior. Owner-scoped pinned host staging and async transfers with explicit event tokens are mock-tested; missing native symbols fail explicitly. Sharded accounting must still query retained allocator handles; PTX semantic kernels and collective CUDA execution remain pending; live-CUDA validation remains open.

entries.subject: CUDA kernel/PTX rendering, profiling and graph replay

fields.Acceptance requirement: Deterministic PTX and mock module/function/cache/launch paths cover exact generic elementwise/static-view semantics, correctness-first reductions for stored dtypes, serial F32/F64 matmul boundaries, shared-memory tiled F32 matrix/broadcast matmul with tails, and exact-tile sm_80+ F16/BF16 m16n8k16 tensor-core matmul. Launch/shared validation, uniform barriers, source maps, and cache reuse are explicit; tiled and tensor-core mocks use independent simulators. Product/extrema retain their raw storage contracts. Tiled reductions, tensor-core tails/multi-warp/async staging, broader generic coverage, and live CUDA/ptxas validation remain open; `NativeDispatch` is unchanged.

entries.subject: OpenCL runtime and OpenCL C rendering

fields.Acceptance requirement: Runtime-loaded OpenCL 1.2 ICD with exact symbol errors, thread-confined RAII resources, checked copies/build logs/owner validation, and capability-aware cache/launch preflight. Static OpenCL C and owner-scoped semantic mocks cover contiguous/broadcast and checked shrink views; Bool/I32/U32/F32, capability-gated I64/U64/F64, and fp64-gated raw F16/BF16 with software exact decode/ties-to-even encode; and staged guarded integer elementwise/reduction execution with generation-safe commit. Captured random plans have a graph-free one-output ABI and immutable source/cache identity: tinygrad Threefry2x32 chunk/carry/low-high packing lowers uniform and paired F32-source Box--Muller normal for F16/BF16/F32/F64, plus F32-uniform affine randint for I8/I16/I32/I64/U8/U16/U32/U64. F16/BF16/F64 and I64/U64 capability failures reject before ICD calls; zero random domains do not submit; mock execution uses the retained plan rather than CpuBackend. OpenCL normal live results are tolerance-only, and no accelerator state reservation is claimed. Dynamic control/reduction axes, broader unary/cast families, runtime-polymorphic views/shapes, cross-thread resources, device-side random state reservation, and broad live-device validation remain.

entries.subject: Metal runtime and Metal Shading Language rendering

fields.Acceptance requirement: SDK-free runtime loading on macOS; `MetalRuntime::discover` distinguishes framework/symbol failure from a process-visible `MetalDiscovery::NoDevices` result; thread-confined RAII device/queue/logical generation-backed typed buffer/library/pipeline/cache/command/transaction/completion ownership; checked copies, source diagnostics, ordered ABI, launch preflight, readiness query, and consuming collection. `CpuSession::realize_metal` is the strict caller-owned-device public path for static F32/Bool/I32/U32 elementwise/select/cast plus checked affine views: it fully plans before resources, returns detached output and handle-free logical cache/capability trace, reuses the caller device cache, and returns exact zero-domain outputs without queue/pipeline/buffer/command work. It has no CPU fallback. Static F32/Bool/I32/U32 elementwise/view UOps and guarded I32/U32 transactional execution have independent typed semantic mocks. Captured random plans have a graph-free one-output ABI and immutable source/cache identity: exact Threefry2x32 chunk/carry/low-high packing lowers F32 uniform and paired-F32-source Box--Muller normal plus F32-uniform affine randint for I32/U32. The release-host probe currently reports no process-visible device despite hardware inventory, so live evidence remains unavailable there. F16/BF16/F64 and 64-bit integer random plans reject before command submission because current MSL storage/capability plumbing cannot prove their contract. Linear/ONNX/model inference, reductions, ReLU and other graph unary ops, broader storage/ops, dynamic shapes/views, effects/aliases, device-resident state, graph capture/profiling, shared/tensor-core paths, multi-device behavior, and broad live validation remain.

Typed thread-confined instance/adapter/device/queue/logical-generation buffer/shader/pipeline/cache/command/transaction ownership; four-byte physical allocation with checked logical H2D/D2H and aligned D2D; bounded build errors; ordered storage-plus-uniform ABI; launch preflight; query and consuming collect. Static F16/BF16/F32/Bool/I32/U32 elementwise/views and staged guarded I32/U32 execution have deterministic WGSL and typed semantic mocks. Captured random plans are zero-input/one-output immutable Threefry artifacts: F32 uniform and paired-F32-source Box--Muller normal plus F32-uniform affine I32/U32 randint use carry-safe chunk and low/high packing, plan/capability/source cache identity, zero-domain no-submit, and retained-plan mock semantics independent of CpuBackend. Packed F16/BF16 random writes are deliberately rejected pending a dedicated validated disjoint-lane protocol; F64/I64/U64 are unsupported. The SDK-free loader intentionally rejects unpinned native callback/future ABIs before calls, so no live WebGPU evidence is claimed. Reductions, broader random storage, dynamic shapes, capture/profiling, multi-adapter execution, and broad live validation remain.
Platform-gated backend suites
Checked owned file byte windows and deterministic null planning traces are tested; file-backed lazy tensors, mmap, and mockgpu/replay parity remain.

entries.subject: JIT capture, specialization, cache and symbolic replay

fields.Acceptance requirement: `CapturedSchedule` serializes concrete schedules or guarded static-rank symbolic families, then replays through explicit interpreter/native/fallback policy without Graph traversal. Complete named bindings specialize checked UOp/schedule descriptors; canonical values key concrete specialization and process-local native compilation caches. Eligible specialized F32 matrix schedules deterministically retile and serialize the selection for PTX consumers; CPU native replay remains serial-K. Symbolic batch preflight validates and compiles every invocation before execution. Elementwise broadcast, static-axis reduction, generalized F32/F64 matmul, source-backed affine movement chains, and exact-splat constant resizing are differential-tested for multiple legal bindings and zero extents. Dynamic rank/cardinality, arbitrary storage resizing, mutation aliases, serialized compiled code, live device resources, and CUDA graph integration remain absent.
Interop and lifetime tests

Graph-composed modules include `LayerNorm2d` and checked-in `LSTMCell` constructor/forward/state/autograd coverage alongside the existing normalization, convolution, pooling, and loss surface. State-free `ReLU`, `AdaptiveAvgPool2d`, and checked `Flatten`, plus graph-free `Conv2d` and `LayerNorm`, participate in the public one-input static `ModuleForward` seam: strict static `Linear → ReLU → Linear`, `Linear → LayerNorm` fresh-state/inference acceptance, and local CIFAR `Conv2d → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear` are covered. `LayerNorm` preserves its existing checked normalized-shape/rank/dtype contract; BatchNorm lifecycle, `LayerNorm2d`, RMSNorm, and other graph-composed Conv/pool/reshape/normalization/stateful signatures are not yet `Sequential` adapters. Tinygrad layout/init gates are tested; dynamic/data-dependent masking and remaining layers remain.

Static host `Muon` joins SGD/Adam/AdamW/LARS/LAMB with checked rank/float/config validation, momentum/Nesterov, and tinygrad-style Newton--Schulz matrix orthogonalization. SGD checkpoint restore preserves its dampening/momentum lifecycle rather than restarting the first-step rule. `OptimizerGroup` and host MultiStep, ReduceLROnPlateau, CosineAnnealing, and OneCycle schedulers have checked state/config contracts. Existing optimizer checkpoints retain config fingerprints, legacy rejection, and strict expected-key loads; LAMB uses corrected bias correction. Fused/device paths, distributed state, and loss/gradient scaling remain.

entries.subject: State traversal, safetensors, GGUF and checkpoints

fields.Acceptance requirement: Explicit deterministic `Module` traversal covers nested `Sequential`, buffers, tied parameters, strict/non-strict reports, fixed shape/dtype replacement, and safetensors round trips. `load_state_dict_strict` is validate-first and delegates successful candidates to the existing all-lock parameter restore transaction, so missing/unexpected/tied-alias-conflicting keys and shape/dtype/lock failures leave every visible parameter unchanged. Bounded strict safetensors byte/file helpers reuse the fail-closed decoder and retain exact keys, shapes, and dtypes without casts or heuristic remapping. The bounded in-memory GGUF v2/v3 reader preserves typed metadata, validates dense and quantized ranges, materializes exact dense storage, and dequantizes Q4_0/Q8_0/Q4_K/Q6_K. Supported rank-two weights may instead be owned as exact-byte `QuantizedTensorData` for artifact/native matmul or validated row gather without eager F32 materialization; the fixed-schema Llama binder uses this path for compatible projections and embeddings. Atomic whole-file F32 mapping remains available and fails on unsupported formats. All other quantized layouts remain opaque; split files, mmap/zero-copy, quantized training, and device loading remain.

Bounded fail-closed default-domain opset-13 static inference import lowers typed/raw initializers; elementwise/activations; movement/indexing/shape; Gemm/MatMul and softmax; Conv/pooling/BatchNorm/GlobalAveragePool; predicate/Where/Clip/inference Dropout; ConstantOfShape; and reductions/args to the CPU oracle. Fixed-F32 named input/selected-output `MatMul → Add → ReLU` fixtures have ONNX-owned opt-in strict-native CPU replay: one canonical multi-output capture uses a caller-owned scalar/vector cache, returns detached deterministically named outputs plus handle-free trace/cache facts, and stages selected same-directory NPY replacements only after native success. A later replacement failure rolls back earlier destinations; composite rollback or cleanup failures remain explicit, so this is fail-atomic rollback rather than simultaneous filesystem multi-path atomicity. Unsupported later native operations, wrong named schemas, invalid selections, and any preflight failure reject before native execution or output staging; no fallback occurs. Fixed schemas mean this native slice has no legal empty or descriptor-invalidation claim. Dynamic controls/shapes, broader Gather/index semantics, control flow, sequences, sparse/quantized/external data, custom domains/opsets, training, devices, timing claims, and live external-model differential validation remain unsupported.

The `datasets` facade and private format modules validate local uncompressed MNIST IDX pairs and exact-count CIFAR-10 binary records. CIFAR label/channel layout, checked lengths, zero records, explicit per-channel F32 normalization, and bounded caller-ordered multi-file concatenation are acceptance-tested; seeded batching is deterministic. `ClassificationBatch` materializes validated caller-selected dense rows in raw storage order, with preserve/flatten feature layouts and integer targets for the static CPU module trainer. No downloads, caching, random crop/flip, or global RNG are provided.

`load_mnist_idx_files[_with_limits]` preflights local file bytes and declared item/dimension limits, delegates exact IDX validation, and returns typed I/O/limit/format errors. Generated-file public acceptance proves deterministic partial batching through `ClassificationBatch`, graph-free Linear/module-derived SGD/CpuModuleTrainer updates, portable fresh-identity resume, exact final state/output equality, and non-mutating evaluation. No downloader, cache, augmentation, device training, or corpus-accuracy claim.

`load_cifar10_files[_with_limits]` uses typed I/O/limit/format errors to preflight local caller-ordered batches, then delegates canonical records to the one parser. `examples/cifar10_local.rs` is the local entrypoint; public acceptance proves U8 NCHW/normalization, final partial batching, a graph-free `Conv2d → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear` fresh-Graph/autograd CPU train path, portable fresh-identity checkpoint resume, exact final state/output equality, and non-mutating evaluation. No download/archive/cache, augmentation, concurrency, device training, or corpus-accuracy claim.

`LlamaPromptWorkflow` and `examples/llama_prompt.rs` compose local GGUF validation, the explicit supported Llama schema, and GGUF tokenizer/template binding into decoded text. The default route uses the existing CPU graph greedy generator. Explicit `--native` selects a separate strict-native single-request greedy route, returning detached token/text data plus resource-free native-stage trace evidence and never falling back to CPU. Fixture acceptance proves CPU/native token/text parity, native-stage provenance, zero-token behavior, context rejection/retry, deterministic CLI parsing, and the existing staged native-cache rollback contract. Native prompt calls do not retain a conversation or serving cache. Generic Jinja, other architectures, arbitrary external-model parity, sampling changes, dynamic batching/shapes, accelerator execution, timing, training, and general Llama-native compatibility are excluded.

`LlamaConversation` and `examples/llama_chat.rs` compose the released workflow/template/generator cache with committed history. Two-turn, isolated-conversation, context-failure, retry, reset, empty-input, and cache non-mutation acceptance is fixture-backed. Greedy CPU/static Llama only; no implicit sampling, shared cache, arbitrary Jinja, device cache, or other model families.

entries.subject: BERT, EfficientNet, RNNT, Whisper and conv models

fields.Acceptance requirement: Checked-in model tests

The checked-in GGUF `SimpleTokenizer` path has typed fail-closed metadata binding, source pre-tokenizer presets, GPT-2 bytes, ordered specials, BOS/EOS/EOT, Unicode/byte round trips, and incremental decoding. Supported `general.architecture=llama` metadata constructs an explicit N-layer dense-or-packed model without whole-state dequantization: norms/bias auxiliaries stay F32, while embedding, q/k/v/o, gated-FFN, and explicit output weights bind dense F32 or exact Q4_0/Q8_0/Q4_K/Q6_K bytes through fixed names, shapes, and orientation. Packed embedding lookup preflights every token and decodes selected rows only; tied output reuses the same exact packed owner and uses blockwise direct CPU or strict native quantized projection without a dense output weight. A serialized mixed-format two-layer GQA/partial-RoPE fixture matches an independently dequantized dense control for full/token/chunk, fixed batches, greedy and explicit-tape generation, continuous prefix reuse/invalidation, and staged-failure rollback. Generic SentencePiece/tokenizer.json, general Jinja/tools/multimodal chat, symbolic/asynchronous/distributed batching, other quantized formats/orientations, RoPE scaling, attention-output/FFN/final-output bias, MLA/MoE/SSM and non-Llama variants, implicit Threefry replay, accelerator packed row gather, accelerators/native-quantized cache arithmetic, and representative external-model differentials remain.
